content:
CHAPTER 1
MEMBERSHIP
I. CATEGORIES OF MEMBERSHIP
The membership of the Philippine Obstetrical and Gynecological Society (POGS) Foundation shall be
in the following categories: Fellow, Diplomate, Junior, Associate, Affiliate and Honorary Member.
A. Fellow – a Diplomate in Obstetrics and Gynecology (OB-GYN) who, after a prescribed period, has
been approved by the Board of Trustees (BOT) upon the recommendation of the Committee on
Credentials and Membership and the Committee on Ethics and Medical Practice (CEMP). All
Fellows at the time of adoption of the 1978 By-Laws shall fall under this category.
1. Life Member – a Fellow who has any of the following qualifications:
a. Reached the age of sixty-five (65) with at least ten (10) years of continuous status
b. Completed twenty-five (25) years as an active Fellow, has applied to the BOT, and has
been approved as such
c. Served the POGS Foundation as President
APPLICATION GUIDELINES FOR LIFE MEMBERSHIP
(for Category B)
Requirements:
1. Active Fellow for at least twenty-five (25) years
2. Fellow in good standing
3. Attended the Annual Convention and Business Meeting for the last three (3) consecutive years
4. Duly accomplished Life Membership Application Form (Appendix I: Life Membership Application Form)
5. Letter of intent addressed to the Chair of the Committee on Credentials and Membership
Administrative Procedure:
1. The applicant shall submit the required documents to POGS office.

REINSTATEMENT GUIDELINES FOR DIPLOMATES AND FELLOWS
DROPPED FROM THE MEMBERSHIP ROLL
These guidelines are intended to ensure that Diplomates or Fellows who were dropped from the roll of members
due to non-compliance with the POGS Foundation’s policies, and who now seek to reinstate their membership with
the intent to resume private practice in the Philippines, are sufficiently updated and aligned with current
competencies and standards of care in the field of OB-GYN.
I. Eligibility for Reinstatement
The applicant shall:
1. Have previously been a Diplomate or Fellow who was dropped from the roll.
2. Signify intent to resume permanent practice in the Philippines.
3. Have no unresolved legal or ethical case related to medical practice.
II. Reinstatement Requirements
1. Submission of one (1) certificate of attendance each for the Annual Convention and a postgraduate
course, with a combined total of 30 PRC-CPD units
2. Participation in a skills-based program (e.g. PRIME Program)
3. Settlement of Financial Obligations as certified by the Committee on Finance
4. Submission of Documents
a. Letter of intent addressed to the BOT
b. Updated PRC license and PMA membership
c. Proof of local practice intent (e.g., clinic/hospital affiliation or job contract)
d. Curriculum vitae and summary of professional activity abroad
III. In cases where there is prolonged absence from OB-GYN clinical practice or where doubt about clinical
readiness exists, the Committee on Credentials and Membership may call for an interview or assessment.

section: Chapter 1 – MEMBERSHIP › II. REQUIREMENTS FOR ADMISSION
content:
II. REQUIREMENTS FOR ADMISSION
A. Fellow
1. The candidate shall:
a. Be a Diplomate of good standing. Good standing means no outstanding annual dues and
must have attended two (2) Annual Conventions over the last three (3) years. In
exceptional cases where attendance at the Annual Convention is not feasible, attendance
at the Midyear Convention may be recognized as a substitute for one (1) Annual
Convention, subject to approval by the BOT upon the recommendation of the Committee
on Credentials and Membership.
b. Have devoted oneself to the practice of the specialty for at least two (2) years.
c. Have good moral values, including honesty in disclosure.
d. Conform with the norms of ethics and professionalism of the discipline.
e. Follow good clinical practice.
f. Be free of any form of litigation or medicolegal issues. However, the POGS Foundation,
through the Committee on Credentials and Membership, may reconsider candidates who
have already served the penalty.
g. Be endorsed as professionally competent and morally upright by two (2) active Fellows.
h. Be invited by the POGS Foundation through the Committee on Credentials and
Membership and upheld by the CEMP and shall be physically present during the
induction at the time and place designated by the BOT.
2. The Fellow status shall take effect on the 1st day of January of the following year.

section: Chapter 1 – MEMBERSHIP › III. RIGHTS
content:
III. RIGHTS
A. All members are entitled to the following:
1. Participate in all official functions of the POGS Foundation
2. Right to vote
3. Avail of Certificates of Membership
4. Receive support from the POGS Foundation for any worthwhile undertaking of professional
nature
5. Receive benefits as provided for in the regulations of the Committee on Mutual Assistance
Program (CMAP)
6. Express grievances against the POGS Foundation, its instrumentalities or any of its members
B. Fellows and Diplomates shall have the right to affix the letters F.P.O.G.S. and D.P.O.G.S.
respectively, after their names, as applicable.
C. Honorary Fellows shall have the right to affix the letters F.P.O.G.S. (Hon.)
D. Honorary Fellows, Honorary and Affiliate Members may avail of the above rights except the right
to vote and be voted upon.

section: Chapter 1 – MEMBERSHIP › IV. PRIVILEGES
content:
IV. PRIVILEGES
A. Members may receive honoraria for services rendered in projects and activities collaborated with
and funded by international and/or national development agencies, societies and organizations.
B. Fellows and Diplomates may serve as official delegates of the POGS Foundation to any
government and/or non-government fora.
C. Diplomates, Junior and Affiliate Members may avail of the above privileges except to be nominated
as BOT or Regional Director.

section: Chapter 1 – MEMBERSHIP › V. DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS
content:
V. DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS
A. The members of the POGS Foundation shall:
1. Maintain the high standards of professional conduct set forth in the Membership Pledge of the
POGS Foundation. (See Chapter on Protocol)
2. Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the tenets and principles of the PMA Code of
Medical Ethics and of the POGS Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct 2025 Edition.
3. Attend at least two (2) out of three (3) consecutive Annual and/or Midyear Conventions.
4. Pay all dues, fees and assessments promptly.
5. Be a member in good standing of the PMA.
B. Regional affiliation of members:
Members shall affiliate themselves in the region/chapter where their main place of practice in OB-
GYN is conducted. This should be included and emphasized in the invitation letter to candidates
for Diplomates and Fellows.
C. An Associate Member, in addition to the above duties and obligations, shall attend at least one (1)
Continuing Medical Education (CME) activity recognized by the POGS Foundation in a given year.

section: Chapter 1 – MEMBERSHIP › VI. DUES, FEES AND ASSESSMENTS
content:
VI. DUES, FEES AND ASSESSMENTS
A. All members shall pay all dues, fees and assessments in the amount and terms as determined by
the BOT.
B. A member with unpaid dues for two (2) consecutive years, despite proper notification, shall be
referred to the Committee on Credentials and Membership for proper action.
C. A member who has retired due to sickness shall apply for exemption from payment of dues;
otherwise, he/she shall be considered in arrears.
D. The following are exempted from paying annual dues and convention fees:
1. Life Members
2. Honorary Fellows
3. Honorary Members

section: Chapter 1 – MEMBERSHIP › VIII. FELLOW IN GOOD STANDING
content:
VII. DISCIPLINARY PROVISIONS
For disciplinary provisions, refer to the Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct 2025 Edition, Article
XII: Enforcement and Accountability.
VIII. FELLOW IN GOOD STANDING
A. Fellow is in good standing if he/she:
1. Has physically attended and has been issued a Certificate of Attendance in at least two (2)
out of three (3) consecutive Annual Conventions and Annual Business Meetings.
2. Is NOT under censure or suspension from membership, as certified by the Board Secretary.
3. Is NOT delinquent in the payment of his/her financial obligations. Delinquency in payments
must be certified by the Treasurer.
4. Has been certified to be in good standing by the Regional Director.
5. Is a member in good standing of the PMA.
B. A Certificate of Good Standing shall be issued by the POGS Foundation upon request.
PROCESS OF ISSUANCE OF CERTIFICATE OF GOOD STANDING
1. The Certificate of Good Standing serves as the official documentation that a member complies with all
requirements for the status as defined in Section VIII.
2. Requirements for Member Submission:
a. Proof of payment of current and previous year's annual dues, ensuring the member is not delinquent in
financial obligations (Section VIII.A.3)
b. Submission of clearance or a certification of good standing from the respective POGS Regional Director
(Section VIII.A.4)
c. Submission of a copy of the Certificate of Good Standing from the PMA and its local component society

section: Chapter 2 – GOVERNANCE › I. PROVISIONS
content:
CHAPTER 2
GOVERNANCE
I. PROVISIONS
A. The POGS Foundation shall be governed by a BOT whose executive arm shall be the Officers.
B. The members of the BOT shall be active Fellows for at least five (5) consecutive years immediately
prior to their election and have not been disqualified under any of the provisions of the Election
Code. Only those who have completed five (5) years of membership of good standing at the date
of the election are qualified.
C. The BOT shall take their oath of office during the Annual Convention.
D. The term of office of the BOT shall commence on the 1st day of January and shall terminate on the
31st day of December of the same year.
E. The BOT shall not receive any salary for services rendered to the POGS Foundation. However,
expenses incurred in the performance of such services may be reimbursed upon the approval by
the BOT.

section: Chapter 2 – GOVERNANCE › II. GOVERNING BODY › A. BOARD OF TRUSTEES
content:
II. GOVERNING BODY
A. BOARD OF TRUSTEES
1. The BOT shall be the governing body and shall consist of at least fifteen (15) members, five
(5) of whom shall be the Officers, and the rest shall be Board Members: eleven (11) from the
NCR, two (2) from Luzon, one (1) from the Visayas and one (1) from Mindanao.
2. The members of the BOT shall be elected by the general membership who are eligible to vote.
The rules and regulations governing the manner and conduct of the elections shall be provided
for in the Election Code.
3. The corporate powers of the POGS Foundation shall be vested upon the BOT, who shall
exercise any and all incidental and implied powers to carry out the objectives in the best
interest of the POGS Foundation.
a. The decision made by the BOT as authorized by the Bylaws is final, subject only to appeal
to the body upon written petition of at least 10% of the general voting population of
members in good standing. A majority vote (50 + 1) by the BOT is required to reverse the
decision of the BOT.
b. The authority of the BOT is almost absolute. However, it is prudent that the general
membership be consulted through a Town Hall meeting on major issues or affiliations,
and on matters concerning contracts or projects. The attendees of the Town Hall meeting
shall include, at the minimum, the BOT, Regional Directors, Chapter Presidents and Past
Presidents.
4. The members of the BOT shall serve for a term of one (1) year and until the election and
qualification of their respective successors. They may be re-elected for not more than two (2)
consecutive terms.

b. A special meeting of the BOT shall be called by the President who shall then announce
the successor within thirty (30) days.

section: Chapter 2 – GOVERNANCE › II. GOVERNING BODY › B. OFFICERS
content:
B. OFFICERS
1. The officers of the POGS Foundation shall consist of the following: The President, the Vice
President, the Board Secretary, the Treasurer and the Public Relations Officer (PRO). They
shall constitute the Executive Committee (EXECOM) of the BOT.
a. All fifteen (15) members of the BOT, sitting en banc, shall elect among themselves the
officers of the POGS Foundation, except the Board Secretary who shall be appointed by
the President. The candidates with the highest votes shall be declared elected.
b. An Officer shall hold only one (1) position in the EXECOM, but may hold other positions
outside the EXECOM.
c. The BOT may create new positions as it deems necessary for the efficient operation of
the POGS Foundation.
2. The rules and regulations governing the manner and conduct of the election of the Officers
shall be provided for in the Election Code.
3. It is mandatory that the candidate for President shall have served as the Vice President
immediately prior to the election.
4. It is mandatory that the candidate for the Vice President shall have served in the BOT for at
least one (1) year within the last five (5) years prior to the election.
5. The President and Vice President shall each serve for a term of one (1) year.
6. Any Officer may be removed from the EXECOM for culpable violation of the Bylaws by a two-
thirds (2/3) vote of the BOT in two (2) successive meetings, and by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of
the general membership in a special meeting.

section: Chapter 2 – GOVERNANCE › II. GOVERNING BODY › C. DUTIES OF THE OFFICERS
content:
C. DUTIES OF THE OFFICERS
1. The President shall:
a. Act as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the POGS Foundation.
b. Act as Presiding Officer in the meetings of the BOT, the Annual Business Meeting and
special meetings.
c. Be responsible for the successful implementation and execution of all the policies
approved by the BOT.
d. Appoint Chairs and members of all standing, statutory, constitutional and Ad Hoc
committees, subject to the approval by the BOT.
e. Serve as Chair of the Committee on External Affairs.
f. Serve as an Ex-officio member of all the standing committees.
g. Serve as an Editorial Consultant of the Philippine Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
(PJOG).
h. Render a report during the Annual Business Meeting.
i. Serve concurrently as the official representative to the House of Delegates of the PMA
and Chair of its Scientific Session in OB-GYN.
j. Represent the POGS Foundation in the General Assembly Meeting of the International
Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics (FIGO), the Asia and Oceania Federation of
Obstetrics and Gynaecology (AOFOG) and the Medical Association of Southeast Asian
Nations (MASEAN) Chapter of OB-GYN, by virtue of the Foundation’s affiliation in those
organizations.
The President shall be given a subsidy as official representative to FIGO or AOFOG
Congress. This subsidy shall cover the following:
1) Airfare: Premium Economy for flights less than 8 hours, and Business Class for
flights exceeding or equal to 8 hours
2) Accommodation: Single occupancy accommodation at the official convention hotel
3) Daily allowance: A maximum of 100 US Dollars per day for the duration of
convention. All expenses shall be supported by appropriate receipts and shall be
fully liquidated within a month after the convention.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › I. DEFINITION OF TERMS
content:
CHAPTER 3
COMMITTEES
I. DEFINITION OF TERMS
A. Standing Committees – are permanent bodies that oversee specific functions, initiatives and
policies within the POGS Foundation. These committees ensure the continuous implementation of
its programs and uphold its mission to advance women’s health and the OB-GYN profession in the
Philippines. These committees report directly to the BOT.
B. Statutory Committees – shall be mandated by the Bylaws or governing documents, wherein the
chairmanship is predefined and not subject to discretionary appointments. Their existence are
required and cannot be altered without a formal amendment process.
C. Constitutional Committees – shall:
a. Be mandated by the Constitution and Bylaws with specific roles essential to the governance
and integrity of the POGS Foundation.
b. Have functions and composition explicitly stated in the Constitution and Bylaws, and cannot
be altered without a formal amendment process.
c. Function independently from the BOT.
D. Subcommittee – a smaller group formed under a parent committee to handle a more specific area,
task, or technical function within the broader mandate of the main committee. It derives its authority
from the parent committee and reports back to it for recommendations, coordination, or approval.
E. Ad Hoc Committee – a temporary committee created by the BOT to address a specific concern,
issue, or mandate not covered by existing standing committees. It shall have clearly defined
objectives and deliverables and shall perform primarily advisory, evaluative or recommendatory
functions. The Committee shall be automatically dissolved upon completion of its assigned task or
submission of its final report. Its term shall not exceed one (1) year, unless extended by the BOT
upon justifiable grounds. Functions requiring continuing oversight beyond one (1) year shall be
endorsed for conversion into a subcommittee or program.

upon justifiable grounds. Functions requiring continuing oversight beyond one (1) year shall be
endorsed for conversion into a subcommittee or program.
F. Program – a sustained, continuing and strategic set of activities or initiatives of the POGS
Foundation designed to achieve specific long-term objectives of the Foundation aligned with its
mission, vision and long-term goals. It is institutional in nature, with defined leadership, sustainable
resource support and periodic monitoring and evaluation. Programs are intended to produce long-
term impact and continuing benefit to the Foundation and its stakeholders. Programs may operate
under a standing committee or directly under the BOT and are intended for continuing
implementation beyond one (1) year.
G. Project – a defined undertaking of the POGS Foundation with a specific objective, scope, timeline
and resource allocation, designed to produce a measurable output or deliverable. Projects may be
implemented under a committee or program, and shall have a designated leadership, monitoring
mechanisms and evaluation processes.
H. Task Force – a special, time-bound and action-oriented body constituted by the BOT to respond to
a priority need, urgent concern or strategic initiative of the POGS Foundation. It is composed of
members selected for their relevant expertise and experience, and is mandated to develop,
implement, and/or operationalize specific outputs or interventions within a defined period. The Task
Force shall be dissolved upon accomplishment of its objectives or as directed by the BOT.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. STANDING COMMITTEES › C. COMMITTEE ON COMMUNITY SERVICE

B. COMMITTEE ON CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES
The Committee shall:
1. Be responsible for setting the standards for the general practice of OB-GYN.
2. Create and periodically update guidelines in the clinical practice of OB-GYN.
3. Formulate Practice Bulletins, as needed by the POGS Foundation.
C. COMMITTEE ON COMMUNITY SERVICE
The Committee shall:
1. Initiate, coordinate, supervise and promote activities aimed at improving reproductive
healthcare, especially in underserved communities/regions.
2. Promote, coordinate and supervise the active involvement of members of the POGS
Foundation in meaningful community service-oriented activities.
3. Provide guidance and support to the Regional Directors on matters related to Community
Service.
4. Seek and receive grants from government and non-government sources to support the
successful implementation of community service programs.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. STANDING COMMITTEES › D. COMMITTEE ON CONTINUING MEDICAL EDUCATION

D. COMMITTEE ON CONTINUING MEDICAL EDUCATION
The Committee shall:
1. Plan, develop, implement and evaluate high-quality evidence-based CME programs that
promote lifelong learning, enhance clinical competence and ensure the continuous
professional development of members in conformity with the current standards of practice and
the evolving needs of the POGS Foundation.
2. Organize CME activities for members and other interested parties, including the Midyear
Convention and other postgraduate courses and scientific meetings in different regions
(except industry-driven programs).
3. Coordinate its activities with the Subcommittee on Scientific Program of the Annual
Convention and the Committee on CME of the PMA.
4. Provide guidance and support to the Regional Directors on matters related to CME activities.
5. Issue certificates of attendance along with the corresponding CPD units to fulfill the
requirements of the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC).
6. Accept grants from government and non-government sources to successfully implement CME
programs.
7. Oversee and ensure the administrative coordination, operational management and periodic
evaluation of programs or initiatives assigned to the Committee as duly approved by the BOT
for implementation:
a. Prompt Response and Intervention for Maternal Emergencies (PRIME)
b. Other future programs which shall be developed and approved by the BOT

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. STANDING COMMITTEES › F. COMMITTEE ON ENVIRONMENT AND WOMEN’S HEALTH
content:
F. COMMITTEE ON ENVIRONMENT AND WOMEN’S HEALTH
The Committee shall:
1. Address the impact of environmental factors on women’s health, promote environmental
health literacy, and advocate for policies that protect both women’s health and the
environment.
2. Formulate and promote activities for the awareness of the effects of the environment on
reproductive health, such as developing educational materials and conducting seminars,
workshops, campaign caravans and other activities for members, trainees and communities
on endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs), climate change and disaster preparedness related
to reproductive health.
3. Formulate strategies on sustainable practices that promote reproductive health through
environmental protection and disaster preparedness to members, trainees and communities,
such as:
a. Environmental conservation practices, which include tree/mangrove planting, urban
farming, coastal clean-up and other related activities
b. Zero waste at home and in the workplace
c. A healthy food system
d. Training workshops to provide maternity and gynecological services in a disaster situation
e. Volunteer registry of members and their safe deployment to disaster locations
4. Foster partnerships with stakeholders as advocates for the environment and reproductive
health.
5. Collaborate with local, regional and international organizations in capacity building for positive
climate action, disaster response and reproductive environmental and developmental health.

H. COMMITTEE ON MATERNAL AND PERINATAL WELFARE
The Committee shall:
1. Develop and implement strategies to reduce maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality
through evidence-based practices and timely interventions.
2. Advocate policies and programs that improve maternal and perinatal care, ensuring access to
quality healthcare for all women and newborns.
3. Organize activities to educate expectant mothers on prenatal care, nutrition, safe childbirth
practices and breastfeeding, fostering early intervention and healthy pregnancies.
4. Conduct two (2) Maternal and two (2) Perinatal Morbidity and Mortality conferences in a year.
5. Have at least three (3) members from the academe and/or Fellows of the Philippine Society

Nationwide Statistics System (PNSS) data in OB-GYN.
2. Formulating rules, regulations and strategies to improve data collection.
3. Furnishing the CHAS and the PBOG with a list of hospitals that have faithfully complied with

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. STANDING COMMITTEES › J. COMMITTEE ON PATIENT SAFETY AND QUALITY HEALTH CARE
content:
J. COMMITTEE ON PATIENT SAFETY AND QUALITY HEALTH CARE
The Committee shall:
1. Set national goals for patient safety, develop an agenda for implementation in accordance with
international standards and track their progress.
2. Be responsible for the creation and dissemination of nationwide tools and protocols such as
Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Team Strategies and Tools to Enhance Performance and
Patient Safety (TeamSTEPPS) to enhance patient safety and quality healthcare.
3. Promote a voluntary, confidential reporting system to detect system weaknesses.
4. Identify persistent safety issues that require more intensive analysis.
5. Conduct at least one (1) Patient Safety workshop per year.
6. Oversee and ensure the administrative coordination, operational management and periodic
evaluation of programs or initiatives assigned to the Committee as duly approved by the BOT
for implementation, such as:
a. Program on Patient Blood Management (PBM)
b. Other future programs which shall be developed and approved by the BOT

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. STANDING COMMITTEES › K. COMMITTEE ON REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH
content:
K. COMMITTEE ON REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH
The Committee shall:
1. Provide updated information on reproductive health and reproductive health-related issues to
members, affiliates, trainees and other interested parties through gathering of literature and
published researches.
2. Formulate activities for the promotion and application of reproductive healthcare services
nationwide.
3. Facilitate equitable access to reproductive health services as embodied in the Republic Act
10354, otherwise known as the Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health (RPRH)
Act of 2012.
4. Have coordinators from Northern Luzon, Southern Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao regions.
5. Oversee and ensure the administrative coordination, operational management, and periodic
evaluation of programs or initiatives assigned to the Committee as duly approved by the BOT
for implementation, such as:
a. Program on Sexual and Gender Minorities (SGM)
b. Other future programs which shall be developed and approved by the BOT

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. STANDING COMMITTEES › L. COMMITTEE ON SCIENTIFIC WORKS
content:
L. COMMITTEE ON SCIENTIFIC WORKS
The Committee shall conduct, initiate, promote, support and coordinate research activities of the
POGS Foundation and its stakeholders. It shall:
1. Identify and recommend to the Editorial Board of the PJOG original scientific works for
publication.
2. Organize and conduct research related activities.
3. Provide grants to members, residents-in-training and fellows-in-training for outstanding
scientific work.
4. Receive grants from government and non-government sources to support the successful
implementation of its programs.
5. Be composed of two (2) subcommittees, namely:
a. Interesting Case Subcommittee
Receives entries and selects the winner/s of the midyear and annual residents-in-training
interesting case contests.
b. Research and Innovations Subcommittee
1) Receives entries and selects the winner/s of the midyear and annual residents-in-
training and POGS Fellows research contests.
2) Receives entries and selects the winner/s of the POGS Flagship Research Project.
3) Oversees the general conduct of research in the POGS Foundation by monitoring
and evaluating researches completed by its stakeholders.
4) Periodically organizes the resetting of the research agenda of the POGS Foundation
following standard guidelines (POGS Unified Research Agenda [PURA]).

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › II. GRANTS FOR INTERNATIONAL PUBLICATION
content:
II. GRANTS FOR INTERNATIONAL PUBLICATION
This will be given to recognized Fellows of the POGS Foundation who have published works in International
Scientific Indexing (ISI) or Medline Journals. It aims to encourage more publications from members and
institutions.
1. For each paper published in an ISI journal – P20,000 pro-rated for each Fellow or Diplomate
2. For each paper published in non-ISI but Medline journal – P20,000 pro-rated for each Fellow or Diplomate,
subject to the approval by the BOT
3. For each paper published in non-ISI and peer-reviewed – P10,000 pro-rated for each Fellow or Diplomate,
subject to the evaluation by the PJOG editor and approval by the BOT
4. For PJOG research articles – P10,000.00 pro-rated for each Fellow or Diplomate, subject to the approval by
the BOT
5. For PJOG case reports – P5,000.00 pro-rated for each Fellow or Diplomate, subject to the approval by the
BOT
6. The paper should identify the institution of the Fellow or Diplomate.
7. The paper should not be industry-sponsored.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. POGS FLAGSHIP RESEARCH PROGRAM
content:
III. POGS FLAGSHIP RESEARCH PROGRAM
Guidelines:
1. Electronic copy (using Microsoft Word or Compatible Software) of the complete research proposal including
a Gantt Chart and itemized budget
2. Prior approval of the research proposal by an accredited technical review board (with names of technical
reviewers/expert panel) and by a separate Ethical Review Board (ERB): the approving ERB must be in the
list of Philippine Health Research Ethics Board (PHREB) accredited review boards
3. The principal investigator must be a POGS member: Curriculum vitae of all investigators must be submitted,
including previously completed researches and ongoing researches.
4. The principal investigator must preferably belong to an institution that shall vouch for the investigator and
shall assure completion of the research project. For independent principal investigators, the Regional
Director will vouch for him/her. A Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) shall be signed.
5. Counterpart funds, including those from private/government sources and pharmaceutical companies, may
be allowed:
a. As long as the fund is declared as an unrestricted research grant (esp. for pharmaceutical companies).
b. The principal investigator (and site investigators) must declare engagement, entanglements, and
conflicts of interest
6. The project should be completed within two (2) years (preferred) and within the budget appropriated.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. POGS FLAGSHIP RESEARCH PROGRAM › M. COMMITTEE ON WOMEN’S CANCERS
content:
M. COMMITTEE ON WOMEN’S CANCERS
The Committee shall:
1. Assist in the formulation, implementation and evaluation of national policies and programs
related to the prevention, early detection and control of women’s cancers, aligned with national
and global initiatives.
2. Coordinate capacity building activities for general obstetrician-gynecologists and primary care
providers in cancer screening, early detection, referral protocols and community-based
management.
3. Collaborate with local, regional, global, governmental and non-governmental organizations
and other international women’s cancer organizations and groups to promote education,
prevention and early detection of women’s cancers.
4. Coordinate with relevant societies primarily involved with the diagnosis, care and management
of women with cancers.
5. Collaborate with local and international organizations to promote fertility preservation in
women’s cancers.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. STATUTORY COMMITTEES › E. COMMITTEE ON CREDENTIALS AND MEMBERSHIP
content:
E. COMMITTEE ON CREDENTIALS AND MEMBERSHIP
1. The Committee shall:

membership.
b. Recommend to the BOT the candidates for Fellows, Junior, Affiliate and Honorary

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. STATUTORY COMMITTEES › F. COMMITTEE ON MUTUAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM
content:
F. COMMITTEE ON MUTUAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM
1. The Committee shall:
a. Be responsible for providing financial assistance for death and sickness to POGS Mutual
Assistance Program (MAP) members as provided for in the MAP manual.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. STATUTORY COMMITTEES › G. COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
content:
G. COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
1. The Committee shall:
a. Manage the POGS Foundation’s funds and provide the BOT with guidance on financial
planning and fiscal responsibility, as outlined in Article XI of the Bylaws.

a. The Treasurer shall serve as the Chair of the Committee.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. STATUTORY COMMITTEES › H. COMMITTEE ON INFORMATION DISSEMINATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY
content:
H. COMMITTEE ON INFORMATION DISSEMINATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY

and activities to members and the public.

2) Newsletter
3) Other media platforms

communication technology.

interactions with members nationwide and globally

a. The PRO shall serve as the Chair of the Committee.
b. The Board Secretary shall be one of its members.
c. The members of the Committee shall be five (5) active Fellows
d. The Chair and the members shall have a tenure of three (3) years on a staggered basis
depending on the year of appointment or assumption of post.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › III. STATUTORY COMMITTEES › I. COMMITTEE ON AWARDS
content:

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › IV. CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITTEES › A. COMMON PROVISIONS

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › IV. CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITTEES › B. COMMITTEE ON BIDS AND AWARDS
content:
B. COMMITTEE ON BIDS AND AWARDS
1. The Committee shall implement procurement processes for transactions amounting to at least
five hundred thousand pesos (Php500,000) and ensure transparency, fairness and
compliance in awarding contracts or acquiring goods and services.
2. The Committee shall:
a. Receive the sealed bid/protected file
b. Determine the eligibility of prospective bidders
c. Conduct the bidding process
d. Undertake post-qualification proceedings
e. Award the contracts
3. Members shall serve for a term of three (3) years on a staggered basis without prejudice to
reappointment, consisting of a Chair and four (4) members, chosen among Past Presidents,
Past Treasurers, and Past Board Secretaries. The incumbent Board Secretary shall serve as
a Liaison Officer.
Note: Refer to the IRR of the Republic Act No. 12009 or the New Government Procurement Act for
guidance on the process of bids and awards.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › IV. CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITTEES › C. COMMITTEE ON ELECTIONS (COMELEC)
content:
C. COMMITTEE ON ELECTIONS (COMELEC)
1. The COMELEC shall:
a. Oversee the organization, supervision and integrity of the election.
b. Administer the Election Code of the POGS Foundation.
c. Be the sole judge of all protests and complaints relating to the election returns and
qualifications of all members of the BOT.
d. Have the authority to postpone, suspend and/or cancel an election for valid reasons as
determined by the Committee.
2. The Chair, in the presence of its members, shall preside over the election of the Officers from
among the proclaimed winners for the BOT.
3. All decisions rendered by the COMELEC shall be final, unless appealed to the appropriate
body within ten (10) days from the proclamation of the election results.
4. The COMELEC shall consist of five (5) members who are Past Presidents for at least one (1)
year before the current election year, appointed by the President with the approval by the
BOT, serving for a term of three (3) years on a staggered basis, without prejudice to
reappointment unless replaced due to incapacity to serve, or resignation.
5. The Chair shall be appointed by the President among the third year members, with the
approval by the BOT for a term of one (1) year.
Note: Refer to POGS Election Code for the provisions pertinent to committee functions, guidelines
and procedures.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › IV. CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITTEES › D. COMMITTEE ON ETHICS AND MEDICAL PRACTICE
content:
D. COMMITTEE ON ETHICS AND MEDICAL PRACTICE
1. The Committee shall:
a. Uphold ethical standards and best practices in medical care, research and professional
conduct.
b. Implement relevant provisions on professional and ethical matters, including the POGS
Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct 2025 Edition. It shall make decisions and
impose sanctions as deemed necessary, in accordance with the Bylaws and applicable
laws.
c. Extend assistance to any active member upon request and provide expert witness from
the POGS Foundation as necessary. (See Manual on the Guidelines for Fellows who Act
as Expert Witness)
d. Provide the BOT and Committee on Credentials and Membership a copy of the evaluation
and final decision regarding the conferment of Fellows and Diplomates.
e. Provide the BOT with a copy of the decision on the censure, suspension or expulsion of
any member for cause, or the exoneration of any member found innocent. The decision
of the CEMP is final and executory, but can be subject to appeal to the BOT within a
certain reglementary period.
f. Actively participate in the CME Regional assemblies to integrate medico-legal and ethical
topics into obstetric and gynecologic practice.
2. The Committee shall be composed of at least five (5) Past Presidents. The Board Secretary
shall serve as a Liaison Officer. The incumbent PBOG and CREED Chairs shall serve as ex-
officio members.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › IV. CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITTEES › E. COMMITTEE ON FOUNDATION OVERSIGHT
content:
E. COMMITTEE ON FOUNDATION OVERSIGHT
1. The Committee shall:
a. Determine the relevance and level of achievement of objectives, timelines, development
effectiveness, efficiency, impact, cost and sustainability of all committees, in relation to
the POGS Foundation.
b. Monitor and evaluate all programs, ensuring that they are in compliance with the
objectives for which they exist.
c. Decide the continuation/dissolution of a project, reclassification of an Ad Hoc Committee
or a Subcommittee, and the integration of committees with similar objectives.
2. For each project, the Committee shall:
a. Review the relevant information, scope of work, project cost and the efficiency of the
output by designing and developing data collection and program evaluation tools.
b. Clarify the role of each member involved in the project.
c. Analyze the work plan and schedule that includes clear milestone dates.
d. Submit an evaluation report to the President regarding the status of the project.
3. A Past President shall serve as the Chair of the Committee and members shall be active
Fellows, and shall serve for a term of three (3) years, on a staggered basis.
4. The Committee shall engage the services of an External Evaluator when deemed necessary.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › IV. CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITTEES › F. COMMITTEE ON INTERNAL AUDIT
content:
F. COMMITTEE ON INTERNAL AUDIT
1. The Committee shall:
a. Be responsible for overseeing financial reporting, internal controls and compliance with
legal and regulatory standards.
b. Examine and audit all accounts related to the revenue, receipts and expenditures owned
by or held in trust for the POGS Foundation and its instrumentalities.
c. Promulgate rules and regulations, in accordance with generally accepted accounting and
auditing principles, to safeguard the funds and properties, and regulate expenditures of
the POGS Foundation.
d. Render an externally audited financial report during the Annual Business Meeting.

G. COMMITTEE ON NOMINATIONS

a. Be the body responsible for overseeing and ensuring the integrity of the POGS
Foundation’s nomination process.
b. Receive and screen the eligibility of prospective nominees for the BOT in the Annual
Election.
c. Follow the standard criteria in qualifying nominees for election to the BOT and ensure
that the required number of candidates is filled.
d. Submit the list of qualified nominees of at least fifteen (15) Fellows from NCR, two (2)

Candidate’s Brochure and publication in all designated sites.
2. The Committee shall consist of five (5) members who are Past Presidents for at least one (1)
year before the current year, appointed by the President with the approval by the BOT for a
term of three (3) years on a staggered basis, without prejudice to reappointment unless
replaced due to incapacity to serve, or resignation.
3. The Chair shall be appointed by the President from among the third year members, with the
approval by the BOT, for a term of one (1) year.
Note: Refer to the POGS Election Code for the provisions pertinent to committee functions,

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › V. AD HOC COMMITTEES › A. GENERAL PROVISIONS

or Diplomates.

section: Chapter 3 – COMMITTEES › V. AD HOC COMMITTEES › B. COMMITTEE ON AMENDMENTS
content:
B. COMMITTEE ON AMENDMENTS
1. The Committee shall:
a. Be responsible for all amendments or revisions in the Articles of Incorporation,
Constitution and Bylaws.
b. Initiate, receive and study proposals for amendment of the Articles of Incorporation,
Constitution and Bylaws and ensure timely submission of proposals to the BOT for
appropriate action.
c. Make certain that all BOT-approved amendments are sent to the members at least sixty
(60) days before the Annual Business Meeting.

members during the Annual Business Meeting.
2. A BOT member shall serve as the Chair of the Committee. Members shall be Past Presidents
or active Fellows duly approved by the BOT.

section: Chapter 4 – PHILIPPINE BOARD OF OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY › I. NAME AND PURPOSE
content:
CHAPTER 4
PHILIPPINE BOARD OF OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY
I. NAME AND PURPOSE
A. The PBOG shall serve as the official accrediting and certifying body of the POGS Foundation.
B. It shall be autonomous in its functions, but is administratively under the BOT. PBOG exercises full
functional autonomy in accreditation and certification matters, while working in administrative
coordination with the BOT for governance alignment and institutional support.

section: Chapter 4 – PHILIPPINE BOARD OF OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY › II. FUNCTIONS
content:
II. FUNCTIONS
The PBOG shall be responsible for:
A. Certifying Examination
1. Formulate the requirements, rules and regulations governing the Diplomate Certifying
Examination and seek the approval of the BOT.
2. Conduct the certifying examinations.
3. Certify as Junior Members those who have passed the Part I (Written) Examination.
4. Certify as Diplomates those who have passed the Part I (Written) and Part II (Oral) Specialty
Board Examinations.
5. Determine the requirements of a candidate for possible re-examination for a specified number
of times.
6. Set the fees for examination and re-examination for approval by the BOT.
B. Hospital Accreditation
1. Set the minimum requirements for accreditation and periodically audit compliance of a
Residency Training Program in OB-GYN through the:
a. Regular/Traditional Hospital Accreditation
b. Provisional Accreditation of Residency Training Programs (PART-P) – a modified and
regulated scheme that uses a stepwise accreditation system. It is considered as Level I
accreditation divided into five (5) phases (PAP 0-4) that will culminate to a Regular Level
II Accreditation.
2. Accredit residency training programs and publish the list of accredited programs annually.
3. Determine the outcomes of the hospital accreditation visit.
4. Set the fees for hospital accreditation for approval by the BOT.
Note: Refer to the PBOG Handbook for details on Hospital Accreditation
C. Formulating additional requirements, rules and regulations that are deemed necessary for the
efficient functioning of the PBOG. These shall be enforced immediately upon approval by the BOT.

section: Chapter 4 – PHILIPPINE BOARD OF OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY › VIII. PBOG CODE OF CONDUCT
content:
VIII. PBOG CODE OF CONDUCT
A. Protect the PBOG and uphold the honor and integrity of the esteemed PBOG at all times.
B. Be circumspect in observing justice and equality towards all, in conduct and attitude.
C. Observe and respect the independence of co-members in making decisions after collegial
discussions by the Body.
D. Guard all decisions of the PBOG and faithfully abide by them.
E. Preserve the nondisclosure agreement on all matters held in trust and declared confidential by the
PBOG and the POGS Foundation.
F. Operate with objectivity, fairness, impartiality and equality towards all candidates during
examinations and accreditation of residency training institutions.
G. Give objective and impartial evaluation of all candidates and hospitals, maintaining objectivity over
and above personal acquaintances or family relationships amongst persons.
H. Serve the PBOG with integrity and commitment, by not participating in activities with
residents/graduates of residency training institutions which may put the integrity of the PBOG in
question.
I. Forego serving concurrently as Training Officer or clinical Department Chair of any accredited OB-
GYN residency training institution.
J. Inhibit oneself from serving as chair of any POGS Foundation committee/subcommittee.
K. Nurture collegiality, camaraderie and mutual respect among the members of the PBOG at all times.

section: Chapter 5 – COUNCIL FOR RESIDENTS’ EDUCATION, ENHANCEMENT, AND DEVELOPMENT › II. FUNCTIONS

The CREED shall:
A. Oversee the implementation of the residency training curricula in POGS-accredited and PART-P
hospitals, and ensure compliance with accreditation requirements for hospital certification and
resident trainee qualifications, including curriculum implementation, facility standards, and
residency competency.
B. Establish a comprehensive evaluation tool for accredited residency training programs.
C. Coordinate with other Committees on matters relevant to residency training.
D. Align with institutions and local or international organizations (e.g., World Health Organization
[WHO], DOH, PRC) on matters aligned with residency training policies.
E. Organize regular meetings, workshops and other tools of training for the Department Chairs,
Training Officers or their representatives on matters pertaining or relevant to the residency training
program.
F. Prepare, conduct and report the results of the annual RISE to the BOT, furnishing a copy to the
PBOG.

deemed necessary.

section: Chapter 6 – INFORMATION AND SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS › I. PHILIPPINE JOURNAL OF OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY
content:
CHAPTER 6
INFORMATION AND SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS
I. PHILIPPINE JOURNAL OF OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY
A. Name of the Journal
The POGS Foundation shall publish its own official scientific publication which shall be known as
the Philippine Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology (PJOG).
B. Objectives
The PJOG shall:
1. Be the medium through which medical research and other scientific investigations shall be
disseminated and have exclusive rights to researches funded by the POGS Foundation,
including ownership, publication, distribution and commercial use.
2. Contribute publications to local and international medical literature.
3. Encourage scientific writing among the members of the POGS Foundation and trainees of
POGS-accredited training institutions.
4. Publish OB-GYN related scientific works which are subjected to peer review and approved by
the editorial board.
5. Be accessible to all members as a digital copy through the PJOG portal in the POGS website.
C. The Editorial Board
1. The Editorial Board shall:
a. Be composed of at least fifteen (15) members
1) One (1) Editor-in-Chief
2) Two (2) Associate Editors
3) One (1) Business Manager
4) At least twelve (12) Editorial Board Members
b. Identify and invite Peer Reviewers of submitted papers
c. Have Editorial Consultants comprising of the President and all the Past Editors-in-Chief
2. The Editor-in-Chief shall be appointed by the BOT from among the appointed members of the
Editorial Board and shall serve a term of three (3) years, starting from the date of appointment
and assumption of office, without prejudice to reappointment for a maximum of two (2)
consecutive terms.

section: Chapter 6 – INFORMATION AND SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS › II. THE POGS NEWSLETTER
content:
II. THE POGS NEWSLETTER
A. Name of the Newsletter
The POGS Foundation shall have an official newsletter which shall be known as the POGS
Newsletter.
B. Nature and Purpose
The POGS Newsletter shall:
1. Be the official publication of the POGS Foundation to disseminate its recent activities and
important announcements.
2. Publish articles / write-ups and columns to maintain a good public image.
3. Disseminate important announcements and activities of the POGS Foundation.
4. Serve as a forum through which members may share updates, opinions and commentaries,
subject to the approval by the Editor-in-Chief.
5. Serve as a medium through which subspecialty and affiliate societies, and international
organizations may promote their activities and services, subject to the approval by the Editor-
in-Chief.
C. Editorial Staff
1. The Editorial Staff shall be composed of at least five (5) members, including the PRO, who
shall act as the Editor-in-Chief.
2. The members shall be recommended by the Editor-in-Chief and approved by the BOT.
3. The members shall be co-terminus with the term of the PRO.
4. The Editorial Staff shall:
a. Publish at least four (4) issues of the Newsletter annually.
b. Provide each member with a digital copy of every issue.
c. Document all the official functions of the POGS Foundation.

section: Chapter 7 – REGIONAL DISTRICTS AND CHAPTERS › I. DEFINITION OF TERMS
content:
CHAPTER 7
REGIONAL DISTRICTS AND CHAPTERS
I. DEFINITION OF TERMS
A. Regional District –
1. The membership in different provinces and cities of the country shall be organized into
Regional Districts based on geographic location for administrative and logistical purposes.
2. The BOT, upon the recommendation of the Regional District and in consultation with affected
members, may create, modify, merge or dissolve Regional District/s based on defined criteria

shall have a set of officers headed by a Chapter President.

are generally geographically adjacent to one another for ease of coordination, headed by the
Cluster President.

exclusively for its purposes and not for the POGS Foundation.
5. Chapter Organization Procedures
a. The applicant shall submit to the BOT the following:
1) A written petition of recognition
2) Three (3) copies of their proposed Constitution and ByLaws
3) List of elected officers
b. The BOT shall appoint an Ad Hoc Committee, to be headed by a member of the BOT, to
study the merits of the petition.
c. The Ad Hoc Committee shall submit its official report to the BOT with its recommendations.
d. The BOT shall act on the petition guided by the official report and recommendation of the
Ad Hoc Committee.
e. Upon approval, the Chapter shall be notified and officially recognized in appropriate
ceremonies presided by the POGS Foundation President.
6. Use of POGS Foundation Logo and Letterhead
The Chapter, upon recognition, shall be given the privilege to create its own chapter logo
provided that the guidelines as stated in the Chapter on Protocols (POGS Logo and Chapter
Logo) shall be followed.
7. Dissolution of Chapter
The BOT may dissolve a Chapter for failure to comply with at least fifty percent (50%) of its
obligations within two (2) years from recognition.

section: Chapter 7 – REGIONAL DISTRICTS AND CHAPTERS › II. ORGANIZATION OF REGION, CHAPTERS AND CLUSTERS › C. CLUSTERS
content:
C. CLUSTERS
1. Organization
a. Clusters only exist in the NCR.
b. A cluster shall be composed of POGS-accredited training institutions that are generally
geographically adjacent to one another.
c. Each cluster shall be Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)-accredited.
d. Each cluster shall have a minimum of five (5) member hospitals.
2. Objectives
The Cluster shall:
a. Conform to the objectives of the POGS Foundation.
b. Promote camaraderie and ethical practice among the members of the POGS Foundation
in the Cluster.
c. Encourage scientific programs and researches.
d. Promote civic or socially-oriented activities among its members.
3. Obligations and Functions
a. The Cluster shall:
1) Follow and adhere to all policies, rules and regulations of the POGS Foundation, in
conformity with Articles of Incorporation, Constitution, Bylaws, Code of Ethics and
Professional Conduct 2025 Edition, and Administrative Manual.
2) Carry out and administer the activities and affairs of the POGS Foundation within
their respective geographical areas in coordination with the national office.
3) Align and implement with the national programs and advocacies.
4) Encourage attendance to all POGS Foundation functions especially the Annual
Convention and Business Meeting.
5) Assist the NCR Regional Director in screening all the candidates for membership in
the POGS Foundation.
6) Remind the payment of the annual membership dues of the POGS Foundation.

a. The POGS Foundation shall recognize the right of the Cluster to impose among its

b. All donations and educational grants in support of Cluster activities shall belong to the
Cluster except those donations solicited by and on behalf of the POGS Foundation. The
Cluster shall make it explicit to the donor/s that such donations to the Cluster are
exclusively for its purposes and not for the POGS Foundation.

6. Dissolution of Cluster
The BOT may dissolve a Cluster for failure to comply with at least fifty percent (50%) of its

section: Chapter 7 – REGIONAL DISTRICTS AND CHAPTERS › III. OFFICERS
content:
III. OFFICERS
A. Regional Director
1. Each Regional District shall be headed by a Regional Director with the following qualifications:
a. An active Fellow or Diplomate of at least five (5) years
b. Practicing the specialty in the region
2. Provisions
a. The Regional Director shall be appointed by the President with approval by the BOT.
b. The Regional Director shall serve for a term of one (1) year, and may be reappointed to
a maximum of three (3) years.
c. In the absence of active Fellows or Diplomates in the region, the President, with the
approval by the BOT, shall appoint other active members to act as the Regional Director.
3. Duties:
a. The Regional Director shall:
1) Serve as the Liaison Officer between the BOT and the members of the region.
2) Establish rapport and cooperation with the members.
3) Implement the different activities of the POGS Foundation through the
Chapter/Cluster officers.
4) Serve as the COP of the region.
5) Act as second endorser of candidates for induction as Fellows in the POGS
Foundation.
6) Serve as the regional coordinator of the CHAS by helping in the screening of
applicants in the region.
7) Coordinate with the various Standing Committees of the POGS Foundation in its
various regional activities.
8) Act as a Co-chair in the Midyear Scientific Convention held in their respective region.
9) Submit midyear and annual performance and financial reports to the BOT, on the
date as determined by the BOT.

9) Submit midyear and annual performance and financial reports to the BOT, on the

10) Be accountable for all funds and other resources entrusted by the POGS Foundation
to the region.
b. All Regional Directors, except that of NCR, shall have the following additional duties and
obligations:

b. Provide information to members on Chapter activities, venues and schedules.

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES
content:
CHAPTER 8
SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES
I. PRINCIPLES / CONCEPTS GOVERNING AFFILIATION TO THE POGS FOUNDATION:
A. Foster spirit of cooperation and goodwill
B. Promote relationships that are mutually beneficial
C. Protect the interest of the general membership
D. Recognize and acknowledge jointly the autonomy of both organizations
E. Uphold honesty, openness and integrity

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › II. SUBSPECIALTY SOCIETY
content:
II. SUBSPECIALTY SOCIETY
A. Subspecialty Society is a society with an accreditation board that utilizes credentialing based on
training and examination given by the subspecialty board.
B. A Subspecialty Society shall:
1. Be a legitimate corporation, institution or organization that is duly registered with the SEC and
recognized by pertinent government agencies.
2. Have only POGS Fellows and Diplomates as members.
3. Have an approved subspecialty training program and/or certifying exams.
4. Adhere to the objectives of and maintain cooperation with the POGS Foundation.
C. The Subspecialty Societies are:
1. Philippine Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology (PSUOG) – 1993
2. Philippine Society for Reproductive Medicine (PSRM) – 1994
3. Philippine Society for Cervical Pathology and Colposcopy (PSCPC) – 1995
4. Philippine Society of Maternal and Fetal Medicine (PSMFM) – 1996
5. Philippine Society for the Study of Trophoblastic Disease (PSSTD) – 2002
6. Philippine Society for Gynecologic Endoscopy (PSGE) – 2004
7. Philippine Society for Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery (PSURPS) – 2008
8. Society of Gynecologic Oncologists of the Philippines (SGOP) – 2008
9. Philippine Infectious Disease Society for Obstetrics and Gynecology (PIDSOG) – 2018
10. Other future subspeciality societies

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › III. AFFILIATE SOCIETY
content:
III. AFFILIATE SOCIETY
A. An Affiliate Society is a duly registered corporation, institution or organization that supports the
POGS Foundation’s objectives and projects.
B. The Affiliate Society shall
1. Be a legitimate corporation, institution or organization that is duly registered with the SEC and
recognized by pertinent government agencies.
2. Be distinct and separate from the subspecialty societies.
3. Have POGS Fellows and Diplomates as members. Non-POGS members shall have special
interest related to OB-GYN.
4. Adhere to the objectives of and maintain cooperation with the POGS Foundation.
C. The Affiliate Societies are:
1. Perinatal Association of the Philippines (PAP) – 1991
2. Philippine Society of Climacteric Medicine (PSCM) – 1992
3. Asia Oceania Research Organization on Genital Infections and Neoplasia – Philippine
Chapter (AOGIN) – 2014
4. Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology Society of the Philippines (PAGSPHIL) – 2015
5. Aesthetic Gynecology Society of the Philippines, Inc. (AGSPI) – 2018
6. Philippine Society for Fertility Preservation (PSFP) – 2021
7. Society for Gynecologic Robotic Surgery in the Philippines (SGRSP) – 2026
8. Other future component affiliate societies

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › IV. COMMITMENT TO THE POGS FOUNDATION › C. CME
content:
IV. COMMITMENT TO THE POGS FOUNDATION
The Subspecialty and Affiliate Societies shall participate in the following activities of the POGS
Foundation:
A. Annual Convention
B. CPG development
C. CME
D. Community service
E. Collection and analysis of PNSS
F. Patient safety policies
G. Other activities requiring subspecialty and affiliate society services

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › V. BENEFITS OF SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES
content:
V. BENEFITS OF SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES
A. Subsidized cost in the use and lease of POGS facilities
B. Linkage with the POGS website
C. Proper recognition in CPG development
D. Other benefits or privileges not stated above but may be approved by the BOT, provided they are
not in conflict with POGS Foundation policies

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › VI. REQUIREMENTS FOR APPLICATION
content:
VI. REQUIREMENTS FOR APPLICATION
A. Letter of intent
B. Documentary requirements:
1. SEC registration papers
2. Constitution and Bylaws
3. Officers and membership
4. Activities
C. A letter of notice shall be given to all the Subspecialty and Affiliate Societies regarding the
application of a new society. The Subspecialty and Affiliate Societies shall be given two (2) weeks
to respond. The BOT shall deliberate and decide on the application. The BOT resolution shall be
final.

section: Chapter 8 – SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › VII. GROUNDS FOR SEVERANCE
content:
VII. GROUNDS FOR SEVERANCE
A. The Subspecialty or Affiliate Society shall be subjected to inquiry and assessment by the POGS
Foundation regarding ethical issues and conflicts of interest between the Foundation and the
Subspecialty or Affiliate Society.
B. The Subspecialty or Affiliate Society may apply for severance from the POGS Foundation.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › I. COMMON PROVISIONS
content:
CHAPTER 9
MEETINGS
I. COMMON PROVISIONS
A. In all meetings of the BOT, PBOG, CREED, constitutional bodies or any of the committees, a
majority of all the members shall constitute a quorum. A majority shall be defined as fifty percent
(50%) of the total membership plus one (1).
B. All meetings shall be governed by Robert's Rules of Order when these are not in conflict with the
rules of the POGS Foundation.
C. Minutes of meetings shall be taken by the Board Secretary if present, or whoever is designated,
and these shall form part of the records of the POGS Foundation.
D. Notices of meetings shall be sent reasonably ahead of time and shall contain the agenda for the
meetings and the minutes of the previous meeting.
E. Routine expenses incurred during the meeting shall be shouldered by the POGS Foundation with
certain limitations as dictated by prudence and prevailing costs. The BOT is authorized to issue
rules and regulations concerning special expenditures of the BOT.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › II. ANNUAL CONVENTION
content:
II. ANNUAL CONVENTION
A. The Annual Convention shall be held every 2nd week of November in the Principal Office (the city
where the POGS Foundation is registered) of the POGS Foundation, as provided for in the
Corporation Laws of the Philippines. Under special circumstances, the BOT may change the date
and the venue of the Annual Convention.
B. The Annual Convention shall have a scientific and business portion and shall be managed by the
Organizing Committee on Annual Convention headed by the Vice President.
1. Scientific Meeting
The scientific meeting shall include the following but not limited to:
a. Presentations of symposia
b. Scientific papers
c. Pre-congress workshops / lectures
d. Scientific exhibits
2. Business Meeting
a. The POGS Foundation shall hold its Annual Business Meeting every 14th day of
November during the Annual Convention.
b. If the 14th day of November falls on a non-working day or is otherwise not feasible, the
BOT may designate an alternative date, provided it falls within the month of November
on the same calendar year.
c. The agenda of the Business Meeting shall be as follows:
1) Call to order
2) Invocation
3) Verification and declaration of quorum (Board Secretary)
4) Reading and approval of the day’s agenda
5) Reading and final disposition of the minutes of the last Annual Business Meeting
6) Report of the President
7) Report of the Treasurer
8) Amendments and resolutions to the Bylaws (Board Secretary and Chair of
Committee on Amendments) (when applicable)
9) Election (Chair of the COMELEC)
i. COMELEC Rules and Regulations
ii. Presentation of the Candidates
10) Other Matters
11) Adjournment
d. All resolutions concerning policies approved in the Business Meeting shall form part of
the standing rules of the POGS Foundation without previous notice.

content:

11) Adjournment
d. All resolutions concerning policies approved in the Business Meeting shall form part of
the standing rules of the POGS Foundation without previous notice.
e. In the Annual Business Meeting, the presence of fifty percent (50%) plus one (1)
members registered in the Annual Convention shall constitute a quorum.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › III. MIDYEAR CONVENTION
content:
III. MIDYEAR CONVENTION
A. The Midyear Convention shall be held in the month of April or May, at such date and place
determined by the BOT. The scientific program shall be prepared by the Committee on CME, in
collaboration with the Region.
B. In every decade celebration of the POGS Foundation, the Midyear Convention shall be held
together with the anniversary celebration at the NCR every 6th of July and/or thereafter.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › IV. SPECIAL MEETINGS
content:
IV. SPECIAL MEETINGS
A. The President may call a special meeting if deemed necessary. This is purely a business meeting
to decide on matters requiring the vote of the general membership.
B. The President is obliged to call a special meeting upon a written petition of at least fifty (50) Fellows
in good standing.
C. The Call for Special Meetings shall specify the time, place, format and purpose/s thereof, and no
business other than that specified in the call shall be considered at any such meeting.
D. Ten percent (10%) of active members in good standing shall constitute a quorum, except as
otherwise provided for in the Bylaws.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › V. BOARD MEETINGS
content:
V. BOARD MEETINGS
A. The BOT shall meet monthly to exercise its corporate powers and duties.
B. A Special EXECOM meeting shall be called by the President to resolve urgent issues that need
immediate resolution
C. A Special Board Meeting shall be called by the President when necessary or upon written petition
of at least three (3) members of the BOT.
D. The Joint BOT meeting shall be held every December to convene the Outgoing and Incoming
officers of BOT for proper endorsements.
E. The Joint BOT-RD meetings shall be held during the Midyear and Annual Conventions for midyear
and year-end reports.
F. All rules and regulations enacted by the BOT may be amended by at least two third (2/3) votes of
the members of the BOT.
POLICY ON REVIEW OF OBSOLETE OR EXPIRED BOARD RESOLUTIONS

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › I. DEFINITION
content:
I. DEFINITION
1. A Board Resolution is a formal, written act and official declaration of the BOT, duly approved during a
scheduled meeting or through an alternative lawful mode allowed by the By-laws. It serves as an authoritative
record of decisions, policies or directives that have a continuing, binding or external legal effect on the POGS
Foundation, its members and its operations.
2. Board resolutions shall be regularly reviewed to ensure relevance and enforceability. Those that are
obsolete, expired or superseded shall be formally retired through BOT action, appropriately archived, and
excluded from active governance references, while maintaining full traceability.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › II. PURPOSE
content:
II. PURPOSE
This policy aims to:
1. Ensure the continued relevance, legality and effectiveness of Board resolutions.
2. Prevent reliance on outdated or conflicting directives.
3. Promote good governance, accountability and organizational clarity.
4. Maintain an accurate and authoritative record of active BOT actions.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › IV. CLASSIFICATIONS OF BOARD RESOLUTIONS
content:
III. SCOPE
This policy applies to:
1. All resolutions passed by the BOT, including policy, administrative, financial and strategic resolutions.
2. Standing resolutions, time-bound resolutions and one-time resolutions with continuing implications.
IV. CLASSIFICATIONS OF BOARD RESOLUTIONS
*as decided by the incumbent BOT
1. Active – A resolution that remains in force and applicable.
2. Expired – A resolution with a defined validity period that has lapsed.
3. Obsolete – A resolution that has been rendered irrelevant due to changes in law, policy, structure or
circumstances.
4. Superseded – A resolution replaced by a newer BOT action.
5. Retired – A resolution formally declared no longer in effect by Board action.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › V. MATTERS REQUIRING A FORMAL BOARD OF TRUSTEES RESOLUTION
content:
V. MATTERS REQUIRING A FORMAL BOARD OF TRUSTEES RESOLUTION
A formal Board Resolution shall be required for any matter that meets one or more of the following criteria:
1. Policy-Making and Governance: Adoption, amendment or repeal of the Administrative Manual, codes of
ethics, election rules, sponsorship guidelines or other policies of general application; issuance of
interpretations or clarifications of the Constitution and ByLaws that establish precedent.
2. Membership Rights, Status, and Obligations: Matters affecting admission, reinstatement, discipline,
suspension, expulsion or other changes in membership status; imposition or modification of dues, fees,
assessments or financial obligations of members; rules affecting eligibility, privileges or obligations of
members or officers.
3. Financial and Fiduciary Matters: Approval of annual budgets and material budget revisions; authorization of
significant expenditures, contracts, sponsorship agreements or financial commitments; appointment of bank
signatories, auditors or approval of financial controls and safeguards.
4. Legal, Regulatory and External Acts: Approval of amendments to the Articles of Incorporation or Constitution
and Bylaws; authorization for filings with the SEC or other regulatory bodies; authority to represent the POGS
Foundation in legal proceedings, negotiations or binding agreements; creation of task forces, committees,
or bodies with delegated powers or defined mandates; delegation of significant authority to an Officer,
committee or third party, including the grant of power of attorney or the authorization to sign documents on
behalf of the BOT.

5. Precedent-Setting, Ethical, or High-Risk Matters: Decisions involving ethics, conflicts of interest or potential

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › VI. MATTERS THAT MAY BE REFLECTED SOLELY IN THE MINUTES
content:
VI. MATTERS THAT MAY BE REFLECTED SOLELY IN THE MINUTES
The following matters may be validly approved and documented through the official minutes of the meeting,
without the need for a separate, formal resolution document:
1. Acceptance or notation of reports
2. Scheduling of meetings and internal timelines
3. Routine procedural or housekeeping matters
4. Expressions of appreciation, commendations or acknowledgments
5. Other non-precedent-setting matters with no material impact on policy, membership rights, finances or
governance

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › VII. GUIDELINES FOR PERIODIC REVIEW AND RETIREMENT
content:
VII. GUIDELINES FOR PERIODIC REVIEW AND RETIREMENT
1. Periodic Review
a. The Board Secretary shall conduct a systematic review at least once every three (3) years, or more
frequently as directed by the BOT.
b. Special reviews may be initiated in response to:
1) Regulatory or legal changes
2) Accreditation findings
3) Organizational restructuring
4) Auditor / compliance recommendations
2. Identification of Resolutions for Review
Resolutions shall be flagged for review if they have:
a. An explicit expiration date
b. Already been fully implemented or completed
c. Conflict with newer resolutions or current policies
d. Refer to defunct programs, positions, structures or conditions; or are inconsistent with current laws,
regulations or standards
3. Review and Evaluation Process
1. A consolidated Resolution Review Report shall be prepared, categorizing resolutions as to be:
1) Reaffirmed
2) Amended
3) Superseded
4) Retired
b. The BOT shall submit its recommendation/s regarding the categorization of Board Resolutions to the
Committee on Foundation Oversight. The report shall include justification for the action on each
resolution.
c. Final disposition will be made by the Committee on Foundation Oversight.
d. The BOT shall adopt the final approval by the Committee on Foundation Oversight.
4. Board Action
o Obsolete or expired resolutions shall be retired only through formal BOT action, duly recorded in the
minutes.

content:

4. Board Action
o Obsolete or expired resolutions shall be retired only through formal BOT action, duly recorded in the
minutes.
o Retired resolutions shall be clearly marked as such in the official resolution registry, with cross-references
to any superseding resolutions, if applicable.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › VIII. DOCUMENTATION AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT
content:
VIII. DOCUMENTATION AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT
1. All Board Resolutions shall be clearly worded, dated, and sequentially numbered, identifying the approving
body and meeting date and certified by the Board Secretary or authorized officer. The Board Secretary shall
maintain:
o A master registry of Board Resolutions with clear status indicators (active, amended, superseded, retired)
and should be color-coded.
o An archive of retired resolutions, which shall remain accessible for audit, legal or historical reference.
Hard copies should be kept for five (5) years. The rest are kept as digital copies.
2. The official Minutes of the Meeting shall be prepared by the Executive Officer and submitted to the Board
Secretary for review. Following formal approval, the minutes shall be signed by the President and attested
by the Board Secretary.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › IX. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
content:
IX. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
1. The Committee on Foundation Oversight shall approve retirement, amendment or reaffirmation of
resolutions.
2. The Board Secretary shall maintain records, initiate reviews, and document BOT actions.
3. The Committees shall provide inputs on operational relevance and implementation status.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › VI. COMMITTEE MEETINGS
content:
X. EFFECTIVITY AND REVIEW OF THIS POLICY
This policy shall take effect upon the approval by the BOT and shall itself be reviewed every three (3) years or
as necessary to ensure continued relevance and compliance.
VI. COMMITTEE MEETINGS
A. All committees shall meet at least once a year. The Chair or any member may request for a special
committee meeting.
B. The meetings of each Committee shall be held at the POGS Building or online. It is advisable to
submit to the Executive Officer the schedule of meetings at the earliest possible time to avoid
conflicting schedules.
C. The President shall be notified of these meetings in as much as he/she is an Ex-officio member of
all Standing Committees.
D. The President may be requested to attend all other meetings by the other entities of the
organization (PBOG, COMELEC, Committee on Audit, CMAP, Committee on Nominations, Ad Hoc
Committees). Compliance by the President is discretionary.

section: Chapter 9 – MEETINGS › VII. REGION AND CHAPTER SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS
content:
VII. REGION AND CHAPTER SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS
A. The induction of the Regional Directors shall be presided by the President during the orientation of
the BOT with Regional Directors which shall be held in January of each year.
B. Each region shall organize and hold at least two (2) meetings a year. One (1) meeting shall be held
during the induction of Chapter Officers and another meeting at the discretion of the Chapter.
C. The Chapters are authorized to promulgate rules and regulations concerning attendance in these

1. The Committee on Finance shall prepare and submit to the BOT a consolidated budget for the
incoming year. This budget shall be approved by the BOT during the 1st quarter of said year.
The budget of the preceding year shall remain in effect until the new budget is approved by
the BOT.
2. Only appropriations approved by the BOT shall be funded by the POGS Foundation.
3. The annual budget may be amended by the BOT, provided that the variance is not more than
fifteen percent (15%).
4. Re-alignment of budgeted funds shall be prohibited, unless in unforeseeable circumstances
(e.g. force majeure), subject to the approval by the BOT. Unused balance of appropriations
shall revert to the general funds of the POGS Foundation.
5. The BOT may authorize the President to approve / disburse a revolving fund per month,
subject to audit.
6. The President, or any member of the BOT, shall not spend more than thirty percent (30%) of
the current assets of the POGS Foundation without prior approval by the BOT.
7. The net income surplus of the POGS Foundation shall be for its sole benefit.
8. In case of dissolution, the remaining assets of the POGS Foundation shall be turned over to
similar institutions.

section: Chapter 11 – AMENDMENTS › I. CONSTITUTION
content:
CHAPTER 11
AMENDMENTS
I. CONSTITUTION
A. Any amendment to, or revision of the Constitution shall be proposed by a Constitutional Convention
/ Assembly, or by the Committee on Amendments and approved by the BOT. Proposed
amendments shall have been sent to each member of the POGS Foundation sixty (60) days prior
to the Annual Business Meeting.
B. Any amendment to, or revision of the Constitution shall be valid when ratified by two-thirds (2/3) of
all active members registered in the Annual Business Meeting, and shall take effect once approved
by the SEC.
C. Whenever any amendment to, or revision, of the Constitution is adopted, such amendment or
revision shall be attached to the original Constitution in the office of the POGS Foundation and a
copy, duly certified by a majority (fifty percent [50%] + one [1]) of the members of the BOT and
countersigned by the Board Secretary shall be filed with the SEC for approval.

section: Chapter 11 – AMENDMENTS › II. BYLAWS
content:
II. BYLAWS
A. Any amendment to, or revision of, the Bylaws shall be proposed by a Constitutional Convention /
Assembly, or by the Committee on Amendments as approved by the BOT. Proposed amendments
shall have been sent to each member of the POGS Foundation sixty (60) days prior to the Annual
Business Meeting.
B. Any amendment to, or revision of, the Bylaws shall be valid when ratified by two thirds (2/3) of all
active members registered in the Annual Business Meeting and shall take effect once approved by
the SEC.
C. Whenever any amendment to, or revision, of the Bylaws is adopted, such amendment or revision
shall be attached to the original Bylaws in the office of the POGS Foundation and a copy, duly
certified by a majority (fifty percent [50%] + one [1]) of the members of the BOT and countersigned
by the Board Secretary shall be filed with the SEC for approval.

section: Chapter 11 – AMENDMENTS › III. PROCESSING AND APPROVAL OF AMENDMENTS
content:
III. PROCESSING AND APPROVAL OF AMENDMENTS
A. Processing and Levels of Approval of the Amendments of the Constitution and ByLaws
1. Initiation and proposal by the Committee on Amendments
2. Deliberation and legal consultation
3. Approval by the BOT for ratification
4. Ratification by the general membership during the Annual Business Meeting
5. Submission to SEC for approval
6. Issuance of SEC certificate
7. Publication of the approved amendments in the POGS newsletter by the BOT
B. Processing and Approval of Administrative Manual Amendments
1. The President shall organize the Ad Hoc Committee for the Revision of Administrative Manual
(ACRAM) every three (3) to five (5) years.
2. The ACRAM shall:
a. Review all amendments of the Constitution and ByLaws and approved Board
Resolutions after the last revision of the Administrative Manual.

c. Submit to the BOT for review.
