to the meeting.

section: Chapter 11 – AMENDMENTS › IV. TRANSITORY PROVISIONS
content:
IV. TRANSITORY PROVISIONS
A. Incumbent Appointee
All incumbent appointees of the POGS Foundation, of its committees, and of its instrumentalities,
shall continue to serve their unexpired terms, unless their positions shall have been abolished.
B. Other Matters
All other matters which may arise during the transitory period shall be decided upon by the BOT.
C. Repealing Provisions
All rules and regulations, policies and pronouncements, written or unwritten, should be consistent
with the provisions of the Bylaws. In case of inconsistencies, the provisions of the Bylaws shall
prevail and the inconsistent provisions shall be repealed, if cannot be harmonized herewith,
amended or modified accordingly.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › I. POGS FOUNDATION LOGO
content:
CHAPTER 12
PROTOCOLS
SUBCHAPTER I
I. POGS FOUNDATION LOGO
The POGS Foundation Logo consists of an outer green circle on a white background. On the outer circle
is the name of the POGS Foundation. The word Manila and the year 1946, which was where and when
the POGS Foundation was founded, is written at the bottom of the circle, separated from the name of
the POGS Foundation by dots on each side. In the center is a white stylized uterus on a green
background, containing a smaller green circle which represents the product of conception. The circle
was chosen because it is a symbol of perfection.
The Logo imparts a visual identity to our Foundation and represents what we are and what we intend to
achieve.
The Logo was presented to the POGS Foundation in the Annual Convention of November 24-26, 1978,
and has been the Foundation’s emblem ever since.
The Hex code for the Green color on the LOGO is #3B8645 (R: 59, G: 134,B: 69). The font used for the
lettering is Helvetica Condensed Bold.
Reference: Abad RS. The Birth of a Logo. Phil J Obstet Gynecol, 3:11-12;1979.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › IV. POGS FOUNDATION MACE
content:
IV. POGS FOUNDATION MACE
The head of the Mace is the shape of an inverted triangle, an ancient symbol for the feminine energy
and the aspect of creation. It is also the symbol of the supreme source of the universe and signifies
intense spiritual aspiration. The vine wrapped around the staff is reminiscent of the serpent-entwined
rod wielded by the Greek god Asclepius, a deity associated with healing and medicine. The vine also
symbolizes life and the POGS Foundation’s aim to continue updating and innovating to better serve our
flock. The five (5) - petalled flower represents the five (5) core values of the POGS Foundation namely
integrity, competence, accountability, compassion and innovation. It is placed at the base of the Mace
to symbolize that the POGS Foundation stands on its core values. The seed represents conception and
fertility, not only it represents conception of life, but also conception of ideas and knowledge. The
dynamic lines on the triangle represents fire. It symbolizes the flame that is our desire to do better and
to be of greater service to our patients which will never falter.
The Mace was designed by Mark Q. Antonio, MD, FPOGS, FSGOP, FPSCPC. It was approved by the
BOT last April 2021, and was first used on November 2021 during the POGS Midyear Convention.
The Board Secretary is the ceremonial custodian of the Mace. During a processional, the Board
Secretary enters first carrying the Mace with left hand extended to hold or support the lower end and
with the right hand crossing his/her chest to hold the middle part of the staff with palm facing the chest.

content:

SCRIPT FOR THE PRESENTATION OF THE PRESIDENTIAL PIN
This is the Presidential Pin. It symbolizes the pride and achievement of an individual person. It is a form of
one’s worth and importance. At this point, I would like to ask Family of Dr. _____ to do the honor of pinning.
[A member of the family of INCOMING will come to the front to do the pinning]
A. Description
1. The Presidential Gavel is a traditional hardwood percussion instrument used by the President
to signal authority, maintain parliamentary order, and mark key procedural events.
2. Component Specifications
a. The Gavel Head is a cylindrical or barrel-shaped body, typically featuring symmetrical
turned accents (grooves or bands) near each striking face, with flat or slightly convex
circular ends designed for high-impact point contact.
b. The Handle is a contoured shaft which tapers towards the connection to the gavel head.
c. The Sound Block is the circular base which features a flat center contact area and is fitted
with felt backing on the bottom to protect resting surfaces, prevent slippage and optimize
acoustic resonance upon impact.
B. Uses of the Gavel and Sound Block
1. During the Leadership Turnover Ceremony (Passing of the Gavel)
2. Parliamentary Procedure and Governance
a. Calling Meetings to Order: The Presiding Officer (President or Board Chair) uses a single
strike of the gavel to open official Business Meetings, Board Meetings, and during the
Annual Business Meeting.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › I. SEATING ARRANGEMENT
content:
I. SEATING ARRANGEMENT
The most important seat is the center and the next is the first seat to the right (1R) followed by the first
seat to the left (1L), and so on, and so forth.
A. Guest of Honor
The Guest of Honor and the President shall occupy the centermost position on the stage or
presidential table. The Host is usually to the right of the Guest of Honor.
B. Office / Rank
The seating arrangement shall generally be based on the office or the rank of the people involved,
except in special circumstances. High-ranking government officials or PMA officers who are present
may be invited to join the presidential table or the stage, but the pre-arranged seating shall not be
disrupted. They shall occupy empty seats at either side of the table or additional chairs shall be
provided.
C. Occasional
In some instances, the occasion dictates the order of seating, as in scientific meetings where the
Guest of Honor occupies the important seat at the presidential table or stage. If there is more than
one (1) Guest of Honor, the President or the Regional Director or the Host Chapter President
occupies the central position. During an Induction Ceremony, the Guest of Honor and the Inducting
Officer, together with the incoming and outgoing officers, are in the main presidential table.

b. The outgoing President shall bestow the Presidential Medallion to the newly inducted

c. A family member shall affix the Presidential Pin to the left side of the President’s outfit.

IV. PROCESSIONAL AND RECESSIONAL
A. Processional

The higher-ranking officers shall exit first, followed by the lower-ranking officers.

A. The Host/Master of Ceremonies or another designated individual shall introduce the personages in

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › VI. COURTESY TITLE DISTINCTIONS

A. Government Officials
1. His/Her Excellency – applies to the President of the Republic, a foreign Chief of State, foreign
cabinet officer, foreign ambassador or other foreign high officials.
2. The Honorable – the preferred title used in addressing most high-ranking Filipino officials in
office or retirees, cabinet officials or those of equivalent rank. The title is also accorded to
foreign diplomats, or those of equivalent rank.
B. National Scientist / Artists
The Honorable – the preferred salutation used in addressing National Scientists / Artists followed
by their full title then their full name.
C. Academic Titles
Types of academic titles:
1. Doctor – medical degree (MD) or doctorate in philosophy (PhD)
2. Professor – academic position in schools or universities
a. If the holder of a doctoral degree is also a Professor, he/she may choose to be addressed
as “Professor” rather than “Doctor”.
b. A President, Chancellor, Dean or Professor with a doctoral degree is usually addressed
as “Doctor”.
c. Those without doctoral or professorial positions shall be addressed as “Mr” or “Ms”.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › I. DEFINITIONS
content:
I. DEFINITIONS
To establish clear governance within POGS Foundation operations, electronic signatures utilized within
the POGS Foundation are categorized into three distinct frameworks:
1. Electronic Signature: Any letters, characters, numbers or a graphic image of a wet signature affixed to
an electronic document digitally (e.g., pasting a signed image into a document or typing a name).
2. Biometric Signature: A method of authentication tied directly to unique physiological traits of the
signatory, such as fingerprint or facial recognition.
3. Digital Signature: An advanced electronic signature created using asymmetric cryptography or Public
Key Infrastructure (PKI) where a unique private key secures identity and prevents undetected
modification after signing.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › II. POGS FOUNDATION POLICY STATEMENT ON ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES
content:
II. POGS FOUNDATION POLICY STATEMENT ON ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES
Electronic signatures are legally binding and confidential. All users are accountable for protecting their
electronic signature credentials and ensuring that signed documents are accessed, transmitted and stored
securely. Any misuse or compromise of electronic signatures constitutes a serious breach of institutional
policy.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › III. SCOPE
content:
III. SCOPE
1. This policy applies to all BOT, members, employees and Administrative Staff of the POGS Foundation
who utilize e-signature for clinical, academic and legal documents.
2. Electronic signatures are fully valid for daily office operations. However, a traditional wet-ink signature
remains strictly required for financial documents and documents needing legal notarization, official
affidavits or specific statutory forms.
3. All technical security measures are strictly managed under the POGS Data Privacy Manual in
accordance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › IV. GUIDING PRINCIPLES
content:
IV. GUIDING PRINCIPLES
To ensure the legal validity and security of all electronic signatures, POGS Foundation adheres to the
following core values and principles:
1. Confidentiality – refers to protection from unauthorized access
2. Integrity – the protection from alteration after signing
3. Authentication – the signatory identity must be reliably verified
4. Non-repudiation – the signatory cannot reasonably deny authorship of signed document
5. Accountability – infers that all e-signature activities shall be auditable.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › V. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
content:
V. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
All POGS Foundation BOT, members, employees and Administrative Staff are individually responsible for
ensuring the proper execution and security of all official signed documents.
1. Protocols for Affixing Electronic Signatures
The signatories shall:
a. Utilize electronic signatures strictly on permitted documents pertaining to official office operations
and communications.
b. Affix electronic signatures only when there is an explicit, written legal authorization (through short
message service [SMS] or email) to the specific transaction.
c. Ensure their electronic signature is affixed only after the final content of the electronic document
has been fully reviewed and verified.
2. The following are strictly prohibited:
a. Pre-signing, embedding signature images into blank templates or unverified drafts, or retroactively
dating an electronic signature
b. Sharing passwords or login credentials used for electronic signing under any circumstances
c. Using personal email accounts or unsecured personal devices to sign official POGS Foundation
documents
d. Bypassing required security logins, verification steps or tracking systems
e. Affixing an electronic signature or signing on behalf of another person without explicit, written legal
authorization

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › VI. TECHNICAL SECURITY MEASURES
content:
VI. TECHNICAL SECURITY MEASURES
1. Confidentiality Guidelines
a. Access Control and Authentication
1) Electronic signature systems shall require unique user credentials (username and password or
biometric identifier).
2) Multi-factor authentication shall be reserved for high-risk and highly sensitive transactions (legal
documents).
3) User credentials shall not be shared under any circumstances.
4) Access privileges shall follow the principle of least privilege.
b. Protection of Signature Creation Data
1) Passwords or biometric data used to create e-signature shall be stored in encrypted form and
accessible only to the authorized signatory.
2) Signature creation data shall never be transmitted or stored in plain text.
3) Compromised or suspected compromise of signature credentials shall be reported immediately
to the DPO.
c. Secure Transmission and Storage
1) All electronic documents containing e-signatures shall be transmitted using secure
communication protocols.
2) Signed documents shall be stored in secure, access-controlled repositories.
3) Encryption at rest shall be required for repositories containing sensitive or confidential records.
d. Audit Trails and Monitoring
1) The e-signature system shall maintain tamper-evident audit logs capturing the identity of the
signatory, date and time of signature, document version signed, Internet Protocol (IP) address
or device identifier.

signatory, date and time of signature, document version signed, Internet Protocol (IP) address

2) The audit logs shall be available only to authorized personnel and retained according to the

e. Document Integrity and Version Control
1) Once electronically signed, the document shall be locked to prevent modification.
2) Any subsequent changes shall require creation of new version and re-authentication and re-
signing.
3) Digital fingerprinting shall be used to detect document tampering.
f. User Responsibilities and Training
1) Users are responsible for securing their devices used for e-signature.
2) Periodic training shall be conducted on the proper use of e-signature, confidentiality and data
privacy obligations.
g. Incident Response and Breach Management
1) Suspected breaches shall be managed in accordance with the POGS Foundation Data Privacy
and Incident Response Policy.
2) Immediate actions may include credential revocation, system access suspension and forensic
investigation.
3) Affected parties shall be notified as required by applicable data protection laws.
h. Compliance with Laws and Standards
1) E-signature practices shall comply with Data Privacy Act 2012, and relevant international
standards (International Organization for Standardization [ISO] / International Electrotechnical
Commission [IEC] 27001; ISO / IEC 27002) including electronic commerce and e-signature
laws.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › XIII. THE FLAG OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES / NATIONAL ANTHEM
content:
XIII. THE FLAG OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES / NATIONAL ANTHEM
A. The National Anthem
1. The National Anthem / Flag Etiquette
The singing of the National Anthem shall always be done during the opening of any program
of importance, be it scientific, socials, business or ceremonial.
2. When Sung With The Flag Undisplayed
The congregation shall stand at attention with hands on the side facing towards the source of
the music.
3. When Sung With The Flag Displayed
The congregation shall stand at attention and looking towards the flag, the right hand placed
over the left chest. The Philippine Flag shall be allowed to move freely and shall not be held
during the singing of the national anthem.
4. The Philippine National Anthem shall:
a. Be played first before anthem of other countries.
b. Conform to the specifications of the National Historical Institute.
c. Be played with dignity.
d. Never be jazzed up.
e. Not be played as a medley; there should be no improvisation.
f. Not be applauded at after playing.
B. Displaying the Flag of the Republic of the Philippines
1. When displayed with another flag from crossed staffs, the Philippine Flag shall be on the right
(the flag’s own right) and its staff shall be in front of the staff of the other flag.
2. When it is flown at half-mast, the Philippine Flag shall be hoisted to the peak for a moment
and then lowered to the half-mast position, but before lowering the flag for the day, it shall
again be raised to the peak.

5. When carried in a procession with another flag/s, the Philippine Flag shall either be on the
marching right or, when there is a line of other flags, it shall be in front of the center of the line.
6. When a number of flags of provinces or cities or pennants of societies are grouped and
displayed from staffs with the Philippine Flag, the latter shall be the center or at the highest
point of the group.
7. When the flag of two (2) or more nations are displayed, they shall be flown in separate staffs
of the same height and the flags shall be of approximate equal size. International usage forbids
the display of the flag of one nation above that of another nation in time of peace.
8. The Philippine Flag shall be carefully protected in storage and in use so that it will not be
damaged. Every precaution shall be taken to prevent it from becoming soiled or torn. Care
shall always be taken so that the Philippine Flag will not touch the ground, water, nor the floor.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › XV. MULTIMEDIA COMMUNICATIONS
content:
XV. MULTIMEDIA COMMUNICATIONS
A. All media communications regarding projects, policies or announcements of the POGS Foundation
or any standing or special committees shall be channeled through the PRO. Releases of local
chapters or regional districts shall be the responsibility of the concerned chapter or region. The
Secretariat shall be furnished a copy of such releases.
B. Such releases shall be correct and proper and in accordance with accepted journalistic practices.
C. The PRO shall be responsible for media coverage of programs or activities of the POGS
Foundation, PMA, AOFOG and FIGO.
D. Statements on controversial issues or issues of national concern shall have clearance from the
BOT before release.
E. Opinions, remarks or comments made by any member not coursed through the BOT shall not in
any way reflect the views and position of the POGS Foundation.

section: Chapter 12 – PROTOCOLS › XVI. MEDIA APPEARANCE / INTERVIEWS
content:
XVI. MEDIA APPEARANCE / INTERVIEWS
A. Invitations for multimedia appearance shall be coursed through the PRO.
B. The PRO shall screen all invitations and make recommendations to the BOT.
C. The PRO shall observe the following guidelines in pre-screening invitations for interview:
1. If the interview seeks information, the interviewee shall observe the following guidelines:
a. Stick to facts or information based on available evidence.
b. Avoid advancing personal opinion.
c. Adhere strictly to the PMA Code of Ethics and the POGS Foundation Code of Ethics and
Professional Conduct 2025 Edition, and avoid using the opportunity to advertise his/her
own private practice, personal techniques, or methods.
2. If the interview seeks opinions or comments from key opinion leaders or prominent
personalities:
a. Discussion shall be based on resolutions passed by the BOT.
b. Personal opinions shall be discouraged.
c. If the subject is about a certain subspecialty, it shall be referred to the proper
subspecialties.
d. If the interview is to feature POGS Foundation as a society, the President shall accept
the interview or delegate to a member of his/her choice.
D. Interviews without prior notice shall not be entertained.
E. For any type of interview, the following guidelines shall be observed:
1. Know the purpose and topic of the interview, and ask beforehand what questions will be asked.
2. Know what company or media enterprise the interviewer represents.

section: Chapter 13 – HOSTING CONVENTIONS IN COORDINATION WITH INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS
content:
CHAPTER 13
HOSTING CONVENTIONS IN COORDINATION WITH INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS
I. THE POGS Foundation SHALL:
A. Bid to host an international convention upon approval by the BOT.
B. Submit at least two (2) years prior to the intended date of the actual convention, or as the
International Society so stipulates.
C. Present in the bid that the date shall coincide with the POGS Annual Convention.
D. Sign a formal contract / MOA as host with the international organization upon successful bid.
II. AD HOC COMMITTEE: COMPOSITION, TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The Ad Hoc Committee shall:
1. Be formed by the President with approval by the BOT.
2. Serve as the local Organizing Committee upon a successful bid for the preparation and
conduct of the convention, without prejudice to additional membership.
3. Prepare a full proposal for the bid and present to the BOT prior to the international
organization’s presentation.
4. Submit periodic reports to the BOT to ensure continuity, oversight and accountability.
5. Coordinate with the Organizing Committee of the International Organization as to protocols
and related matters.
6. Collaborate with local Organizing Committee of the Annual Convention of the year being
hosted.
B. The BOT shall retain overall authority over the international convention based on the guidelines of
both organizations, including approval of major decisions, policies and financial arrangements,
upon the recommendation of the Ad Hoc Committee constituted for this purpose.

section: Chapter 13 – HOSTING CONVENTIONS IN COORDINATION WITH INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS › III. FINANCES
content:

both organizations, including approval of major decisions, policies and financial arrangements,
upon the recommendation of the Ad Hoc Committee constituted for this purpose.

An agreement shall be forged between POGS Foundation and the international organization’s EXECOM
regarding the projected revenue from the convention.

section: Chapter 14 – COLLABORATION WITH LOCAL / SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES › I. RESPONSIBILITY OF THE SUBSPECIALTY AND AFFILIATE SOCIETIES

B. Be endorsed by the POGS Foundation through the BOT upon the approval of the proposal.

F. Comply with all necessary documents for the undertaking with the POGS Foundation.

content:
